attrs.label: A B2B SEO strategy built around the buyer journey

A B2B SEO strategy built around the buyer journey

B2B buyers search differently at each stage. We map the searches to each stage and build the page that wins it, with most of the effort where buyers are closest to a decision.

  1. Stage 1

    Problem aware

    They know something is wrong, not what fixes it.

    They search

    • how to manage client approvals
    • agency project delays

    Pages that win

  2. Stage 2

    Solution aware

    They know the kind of product or service they need.

    They search

    • b2b approval tool

    Pages that win

    Use-case and solution pages

  3. Stage 3

    Comparing vendors

    They have a shortlist and want the differences.

    They search

    • kestrel vs asana

    Pages that win

  4. Stage 4

Most agencies start at stage 1, with blog posts. We start at stages 3 and 4, where the searches are fewer but closest to revenue.

attrs.label: B2B and SaaS SEO services, built for how you sell
attrs.html:
B2B and SaaS SEO services, built for how you sell

B2B services firms and SaaS companies need different pages to rank and convert. Choose yours.

Service and solution pages

Most B2B websites describe everything they do on one long services page. Buyers don’t search that way: they search for the specific service, or the problem they need solved. We build a page for each one, written for the people who sign off the budget, with the proof and the next step they need.

What we do

  • A page for each service, and for each problem it solves
  • Written around buyer objections, not a list of features
  • Proof on the page: results, client logos, certifications and quotes
  • A clear next step: a call, a demo or an assessment
  • Linked from related articles and industry pages
  • Service and FAQ schema, so search and AI tools understand the offer

Example pages/services/regulatory-consulting/ · /solutions/vendor-risk/

What you getPages that rank for what buyers search, and turn readers into enquiries.

Industry pages

A bank, a hospital and a manufacturer buy the same service for different reasons, in different words. Industry pages speak each sector’s language, show proof from that sector, and rank for the searches buyers in it actually make.

What we do

  • A page for every sector you sell into
  • The terms, regulations and roles that sector uses
  • Case studies and logos from the same industry
  • Questions buyers in that sector ask, answered on the page
  • Links to the services each sector buys most
  • Leads from each industry tracked separately

Example pages/industries/healthcare/ · /industries/financial-services/

What you getMore qualified leads from the sectors you most want to win.

Thought leadership

B2B buyers trust people who clearly know the field. We interview your experts, then write articles and guides in their voice: opinions, frameworks and lessons you can’t find anywhere else. It’s the content that earns links, gets cited by AI tools and gets forwarded around the buying committee.

What we do

  • Topics taken from real sales calls and customer questions
  • Interviews with your experts, written up by our writers
  • Author profiles that show who stands behind the advice
  • Original data, frameworks and points of view
  • Outreach to earn links and mentions from industry sites
  • Updated every year, so it keeps ranking

Example pages/insights/ · /guides/ · author pages

What you getA reputation as the expert in your field, and links that lift every page.

Lead magnets

Most B2B buyers aren’t ready for a sales call on their first visit. A useful report, calculator or template gives them a reason to share their details now, so your team can follow up when they are ready.

What we do

  • Reports, calculators, templates and checklists
  • Landing pages built to rank, not just to collect emails
  • Gated or open, decided asset by asset
  • Connected to your CRM and nurture emails
  • Download source tracked through to the deal
  • Promoted from related articles and service pages

Example pages/resources/benchmark-report/ · /tools/roi-calculator/

What you getA steady flow of named leads from people who aren’t ready to talk yet.

Case study pages

Case studies are what convince the buying committee, but they’re often buried in PDFs. We turn them into pages that rank for your services and industries, follow a clear problem, approach and result, and get linked from everywhere they’re relevant.

What we do

  • One page per case study, not a PDF
  • Problem, approach and results, with numbers where you have them
  • Client quotes and the people involved
  • Filtered by industry and service
  • Linked from every matching service and industry page
  • Schema, so the results can appear in search and AI answers

Example pages/case-studies/ · /case-studies/freight-platform-migration/

What you getProof in front of buyers at the moment they’re deciding.

Technical SEO and site structure

B2B websites grow piece by piece: a new section here, a microsite there. We bring it into one clear structure, so Google sees how your services, industries and content fit together, and every important page gets crawled, indexed and found.

What we do

  • A structure built around services, industries and resources
  • Crawling and indexing problems found and fixed
  • Microsites and subdomains brought onto the main site
  • Fast pages on every device
  • Redesigns and migrations without lost rankings
  • Schema for your organisation, services and people

Example pagesSite structure · Search Console · server and CMS settings

What you getA site where every important page can rank.

Feature and use-case pages

Buyers search for the job they need done, not your product’s name. A page for each feature and each use case meets them there, shows the product doing that job, and links to the plan that fits.

What we do

  • A page for each feature, and each team or industry that uses it
  • Screenshots and short videos of the product in use
  • Written from real customer conversations
  • Links to pricing, integrations and sign-up
  • Use-case pages for each job title you sell to
  • Updated when the product changes

Example pages/features/approvals/ · /use-cases/agency-workflows/

What you getRankings for the problems your product solves, not just your brand.

Comparison and alternatives pages

Someone searching “you vs competitor” or “competitor alternatives” is about to choose. These pages convert better than almost anything else in SaaS, as long as they’re honest. We write them fairly, with real differences and a clear reason to pick you.

What we do

  • “You vs competitor” pages for every main rival
  • “Competitor alternatives” pages that include you, with proof
  • Side-by-side tables based on real product use
  • An honest “choose them if…” section that builds trust
  • Migration help and switching offers
  • Kept up to date as competitors change pricing and features

Example pages/compare/kestrel-vs-asana/ · /alternatives/monday/

What you getDemos from buyers who already have a shortlist.

Integration pages

Every tool your product connects to is a search: “Salesforce workflow integration”, “Slack approvals”. A page for each integration ranks for those searches and answers IT’s first question: will it work with our stack?

What we do

  • A page for every integration and partner
  • What syncs, in which direction, and how to set it up
  • Use cases for each integration
  • Partner directory listings that link back
  • A searchable integrations hub
  • Built from a template, so new ones go live fast

Example pages/integrations/salesforce/ · /integrations/slack/

What you getTraffic from the tools your buyers already use every day.

Programmatic SEO

Templates, integrations, locations or data you already have can become hundreds of useful pages. We design the template, the data and the rules that keep every page worth ranking, so you get scale without thin or duplicate content.

What we do

  • Opportunities found in your product data and search demand
  • Page templates designed with your product team
  • Unique, useful content on every page, not swapped keywords
  • Rules for what gets published, and what gets noindexed
  • Internal linking between related pages
  • Indexing watched page by page in Search Console

Example pages/templates/client-onboarding/ · /integrations/{tool}/

What you getSearch traffic at a scale hand-built pages can’t reach.

Product-led content

The best SaaS articles teach something and show the product doing it. We write how-tos and guides around real workflows in your product, with screenshots, so readers learn and see why they’d want it.

What we do

  • Topics where your product is the natural answer
  • Real workflows with screenshots from your product
  • Written by people who’ve used the product
  • Calls to action that match where the reader is
  • Links to features, templates and sign-up
  • Tracked to trials and demos, not just page views

Example pages/blog/automate-client-approvals/ · /guides/

What you getReaders who become trials, because they’ve seen it work.

Free tools and templates

A free calculator, generator or template library can bring in thousands of the right people every month, and introduce them to your product. We plan, design and launch them with your team, and make sure they rank.

What we do

  • Ideas tested against real search demand
  • Simple tools built with your developers
  • Template libraries with a page per template
  • Sign-up offered at the right moment, not up front
  • Links earned from people who share the tool
  • Usage and sign-ups tracked in your analytics

Example pages/tools/project-cost-calculator/ · /templates/

What you getA steady source of sign-ups that keeps working for years.

attrs.label: SaaS technical SEO, done by developers
attrs.html:
SaaS technical SEO, done by developers

SaaS websites break SEO in ways other sites don’t. They’re built with JavaScript frameworks, split across app, blog and docs, and change with every release. Our developers find the problems in the code and fix them there, working alongside your product team.

JavaScript rendering

Many SaaS marketing sites are built with the same JavaScript frameworks as the product. The page looks perfect to a visitor, but the HTML the server sends is almost empty. Google has to queue the page, run the JavaScript and come back, which can take days, and sometimes key content, links or metadata never make it into the index.

What we do

  • Compare the raw HTML with the rendered page on every template
  • Server-side rendering or static generation for pages that should rank
  • Titles, meta, canonicals and links in the first HTML response
  • Client-side routing that still gives every page a real, crawlable URL
  • Test with Search Console’s URL inspection and a JavaScript-off crawl
  • Work with your developers in pull requests, not in a PDF

Tools we useNext.js · Nuxt · Gatsby · Screaming Frog (JavaScript rendering) · Search Console URL inspection

What you getEvery marketing page fully indexed on the first crawl, with all its content and links.

App and marketing site

A SaaS company usually runs several sites: the marketing site, a blog, docs, a help centre, the app and a staging copy. Without a plan, login screens and staging pages end up in Google, while the blog and docs build authority on separate subdomains that never helps the pages that sell.

What we do

  • Map every subdomain and decide which ones should rank
  • App, login and staging kept out of the index, safely
  • Blog and docs moved to folders on the main domain where it helps
  • Redirects, canonicals and sitemaps for every move
  • One Search Console set-up that covers every property
  • Internal links between the marketing site, blog and docs

Tools we useSearch Console domain property · robots.txt · server and CDN rules

What you getOne strong domain, and only the pages that should rank in Google.

Docs and help centres

Your help articles answer exactly the questions buyers and users search for: “how to set up approval rules”, “connect to Salesforce”. On a hosted help centre, those pages are often slow, unlinked and ignored by Google, and they never send readers to the features or sign-up.

What we do

  • Help centre structure and URLs that Google can crawl
  • Titles and headings that match how people search
  • Links from each article to the feature it describes
  • A trial or demo call to action for readers who aren’t customers
  • FAQ and HowTo-style structure where it fits
  • Old and duplicate articles merged or retired

Tools we useZendesk Guide · Intercom Articles · GitBook · Mintlify · HubSpot Knowledge Base

What you getHelp articles that rank, help users, and bring in new trials.

Sign-up and pricing pages

Pricing and sign-up pages get the most valuable visits on the site, but they are often slow, missing from Google, or not tracked as conversions. If you can’t see which landing pages lead to trials and demos, you can’t tell what SEO is worth.

What we do

  • Pricing pages indexable, fast and kept up to date
  • Sign-up flows that don’t block or confuse Googlebot
  • Trials, demos and sign-ups tracked as key events in GA4
  • Landing page and first touch passed to the CRM
  • Pricing FAQs answered on the page, with markup
  • A/B tests set up so they don’t create duplicate pages

Tools we useGoogle Analytics 4 · Tag Manager · HubSpot or Salesforce · PostHog

What you getClear numbers on which pages bring in trials, demos and revenue.

Programmatic pages

Generated pages can bring in thousands of visits, or drag the whole site down. When hundreds of pages are almost the same, Google crawls them, decides they aren’t worth indexing and starts trusting the rest of the site less.

What we do

  • Rules for which pages are published, and which stay out of the index
  • Unique content and data on every page, not swapped keywords
  • Canonicals for near-duplicates
  • Sitemaps split by template, so indexing can be tracked
  • Internal links from hubs and related pages
  • Thin pages improved, merged or removed

Tools we useSearch Console page indexing · sitemaps by template · Screaming Frog

What you getHundreds of pages in Google, each one worth ranking.

Page speed

SaaS marketing sites collect scripts: live chat, tag managers with dozens of tags, A/B testing, session recording, review widgets and web fonts. Each one slows the page, and together they fail Core Web Vitals on mobile.

What we do

  • Every script measured, with its cost on the main thread
  • Tags removed, delayed or loaded only where they’re used
  • Images, fonts and video optimised and sized correctly
  • Caching and a CDN set up for marketing pages
  • Performance budgets in your build, so it stays fast
  • Core Web Vitals tracked for each page template

Tools we usePageSpeed Insights · Chrome DevTools · WebPageTest · Search Console Core Web Vitals

What you getFast pages that pass Core Web Vitals, and buyers who don’t leave.

Product schema

Search and AI tools need structured data to understand what your product is, what it costs and what customers think. With it, your pages can show ratings and prices in Google, and AI answers describe you correctly.

What we do

  • SoftwareApplication or Product markup with pricing
  • Review ratings from your review platforms, where allowed
  • Organization, logo and social profiles
  • FAQ markup where the questions are on the page
  • Breadcrumbs across the site, blog and docs
  • Every change checked in the Rich Results Test

Tools we useJSON-LD in templates · Rich Results Test · Schema Markup Validator

What you getRicher results in Google, and AI answers that get your product right.

Releases and redesigns

SaaS sites change every week. A renamed page, a new framework or a redesign can quietly remove pages from Google, and nobody notices until the demos slow down.

What we do

  • SEO checks added to pull requests and your build
  • Redirect maps for every removed or renamed URL
  • Staging kept out of Google, production never noindexed
  • Launch-day checks on robots.txt, sitemaps and analytics
  • Rankings and traffic watched for weeks after a launch
  • Help for your developers when something fails

Tools we useGitHub Actions or GitLab CI · Lighthouse CI · Screaming Frog scheduled crawls

What you getReleases that ship without losing the rankings you’ve earned.

Need a full check first? See our technical SEO audit.

attrs.title: B2B and SaaS SEO questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: What is B2B SEO?
items.answer: B2B SEO helps businesses that sell to other businesses get found by the people researching and buying what they offer. It targets fewer, higher-value searches, speaks to the whole buying committee and is measured in demos, pipeline and revenue.

items.question: How is B2B SEO different from B2C SEO?
items.answer: B2B searches are fewer but worth far more, sales cycles are longer, and several people research before a decision. B2B SEO focuses on comparison, solution and proof pages, and on reporting that ties search to revenue.

items.question: How is SaaS SEO different from B2B SEO?
items.answer: SaaS SEO adds product-led pages: features, integrations, comparisons, alternatives and programmatic pages, plus technical work on JavaScript sites, docs and sign-up flows.

items.question: How much do B2B SEO services cost?
items.answer: It depends on your market, site and how much content you need. Every plan is a fixed monthly price, quoted after a free 30-minute call.

items.question: How long does B2B SEO take to work?
items.answer: Bottom-of-funnel pages can start bringing in demos within three months. A full programme usually builds over six to twelve months.

items.question: Can you connect SEO to our CRM?
items.answer: Yes. We work with HubSpot, Salesforce and other CRMs to track organic leads from first visit to closed deal.

items.question: Do you use AI to write content?
items.answer: No. Every page is written and proofread by people. We use AI only for research, and to learn what content AI search tools cite.

items.question: Do you work with early-stage SaaS companies?
items.answer: Yes. Our Foundation plan is built for seed and early-stage SaaS and smaller B2B firms that need the basics right first.
